# ASP.NET Core MVC?

## Basic

**What is ASP.NET Core MVC?**

ASP.NET Core MVC is a web framework for building dynamic websites using the **Model-View-Controller** pattern. Think of it like Flutter for web, but server-side rendered instead of client-side.

### The MVC Pattern

```
     User Request
          ↓
    ┌─────────────┐
    │ Controller  │  ← Brain: Handles requests
    └─────────────┘     & coordinates everything
          ↓ ↑
    ┌─────────────┐
    │    Model    │  ← Data: Your business logic
    └─────────────┘     & data structures
          ↓
    ┌─────────────┐
    │    View     │  ← UI: HTML templates
    └─────────────┘     (like Flutter widgets)
          ↓
     HTML Response
```

### Let's Build a Simple Book Library App

#### Create Your First Project

```bash
# Create a new MVC project
dotnet new mvc -n BookLibrary
cd BookLibrary

# Run it
dotnet run
```

Visit `http://localhost:5000` (or the port shown) - you'll see a default website!

#### Project Structure

```
BookLibrary/
├── Controllers/          # Handle HTTP requests (like Flutter controllers)
│   └── HomeController.cs
├── Models/              # Data classes (like Dart models)
├── Views/               # HTML templates
│   ├── Home/
│   │   └── Index.cshtml
│   └── Shared/          # Reusable components
│       └── _Layout.cshtml
├── wwwroot/            # Static files (CSS, JS, images)
├── Program.cs          # Entry point (like main() in Dart)
└── appsettings.json    # Configuration
```

#### Create a Model

Create `Models/Book.cs`:

```csharp
namespace BookLibrary.Models;

public class Book
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public string Title { get; set; } = "";
    public string Author { get; set; } = "";
    public int Year { get; set; }
    
    // Constructor (optional with C# 9+)
    public Book(int id, string title, string author, int year)
    {
        Id = id;
        Title = title;
        Author = author;
        Year = year;
    }
}
```

*Similar to Dart classes, but using Properties instead of fields*

#### Create a Controller

Create `Controllers/BookController.cs`:

```csharp
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using BookLibrary.Models;

namespace BookLibrary.Controllers;

public class BookController : Controller
{
    // Fake database (in real apps, use Entity Framework)
    private static List<Book> _books = new()
    {
        new Book(1, "The Pragmatic Programmer", "Andy Hunt", 1999),
        new Book(2, "Clean Code", "Robert Martin", 2008),
        new Book(3, "Design Patterns", "Gang of Four", 1994)
    };

    // GET: /Book/
    public IActionResult Index()
    {
        return View(_books);  // Pass model to view
    }

    // GET: /Book/Details/1
    public IActionResult Details(int id)
    {
        var book = _books.FirstOrDefault(b => b.Id == id);
        if (book == null)
            return NotFound();
        
        return View(book);
    }

    // GET: /Book/Create
    public IActionResult Create()
    {
        return View();
    }

    // POST: /Book/Create
    [HttpPost]
    public IActionResult Create(Book book)
    {
        if (ModelState.IsValid)  // Validation check
        {
            book.Id = _books.Max(b => b.Id) + 1;
            _books.Add(book);
            return RedirectToAction("Index");
        }
        return View(book);
    }
}
```

#### Create Views

Create folder `Views/Book/` and add these files:

**Views/Book/Index.cshtml** (List all books):
```html
@model List<Book>

<h1>📚 Book Library</h1>

<a asp-action="Create" class="btn btn-primary">Add New Book</a>

<table class="table mt-3">
    <thead>
        <tr>
            <th>Title</th>
            <th>Author</th>
            <th>Year</th>
            <th>Actions</th>
        </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
        @foreach (var book in Model)
        {
            <tr>
                <td>@book.Title</td>
                <td>@book.Author</td>
                <td>@book.Year</td>
                <td>
                    <a asp-action="Details" asp-route-id="@book.Id">View</a>
                </td>
            </tr>
        }
    </tbody>
</table>
```

**Views/Book/Details.cshtml** (Show one book):
```html
@model Book

<h1>@Model.Title</h1>
<dl>
    <dt>Author:</dt>
    <dd>@Model.Author</dd>
    
    <dt>Year:</dt>
    <dd>@Model.Year</dd>
</dl>

<a asp-action="Index">Back to List</a>
```

**Views/Book/Create.cshtml** (Form to add book):
```html
@model Book

<h1>Add New Book</h1>

<form asp-action="Create" method="post">
    <div class="mb-3">
        <label asp-for="Title">Title</label>
        <input asp-for="Title" class="form-control" />
    </div>
    
    <div class="mb-3">
        <label asp-for="Author">Author</label>
        <input asp-for="Author" class="form-control" />
    </div>
    
    <div class="mb-3">
        <label asp-for="Year">Year</label>
        <input asp-for="Year" class="form-control" />
    </div>
    
    <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Save</button>
    <a asp-action="Index" class="btn btn-secondary">Cancel</a>
</form>
```

#### Add Navigation

In `Views/Shared/_Layout.cshtml`, add a menu item (around line 25):
```html
<li class="nav-item">
    <a class="nav-link text-dark" asp-controller="Book" asp-action="Index">Books</a>
</li>
```

**Run and Test!**

```bash
dotnet run
```

Navigate to `http://localhost:5000/Book` to see your library!

### Key Concepts Explained

#### Routing
```
URL Pattern: /{Controller}/{Action}/{id?}

/Book/Index     → BookController.Index()
/Book/Details/5 → BookController.Details(5)
/Book/Create    → BookController.Create()
```

#### Tag Helpers
```html
<!-- These special attributes generate URLs -->
<a asp-controller="Book" asp-action="Index">
<!-- Becomes: <a href="/Book/Index"> -->

<input asp-for="Title" />
<!-- Becomes: <input name="Title" id="Title" /> -->
```

#### Data Flow
```
1. User clicks "Add Book"
        ↓
2. GET /Book/Create
        ↓
3. BookController.Create() returns View()
        ↓
4. Create.cshtml renders form
        ↓
5. User fills form & submits
        ↓
6. POST /Book/Create with form data
        ↓
7. BookController.Create(Book book) processes
        ↓
8. Redirect to Index
```

### Coming from Dart/Flutter

| Flutter/Dart | ASP.NET Core MVC |
|-------------|------------------|
| StatelessWidget | View (cshtml) |
| State management | Controller |
| Model classes | Model classes |
| Navigator.push() | RedirectToAction() |
| Widget tree | HTML DOM |
| Hot reload | Hot reload (dotnet watch) |

### Next Steps

1. **Entity Framework Core**: Database ORM (like sqflite but more powerful)
2. **Dependency Injection**: Built-in DI container
3. **Authentication**: Identity framework
4. **API**: Create REST APIs with controllers
5. **Razor Pages**: Simpler alternative to MVC for page-focused apps
